title: Flows and shortest paths in plane graphs, with machine programs including the maximum-flow algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen, in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of maximum flows and shortest paths. Plane graphs are combinatorial maps (darts with a reversal, a tail vertex, a face and a next dart along the face boundary) whose graph and dual are connected and which satisfy Euler's formula V + F = D/2 + 2. The machine statements are about one explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run) and fixed encodings of the inputs as lists of natural numbers; each asserts one fixed program for all inputs. Six theorems are compared: (1) the max-flow min-cut theorem for a network with nonnegative integer capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks: some flow and some cut have equal value and capacity, so the flow is maximum and the cut minimum; (2) the theorem of Miller and Naor: on a plane map, given an antisymmetric g with net outflow b at every vertex, a b-flow within the capacities u exists if and only if the dual graph with lengths u - g has a feasible potential; (3) a program decides, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map with V vertices, F faces and S darts, natural capacities, supplies and demands, whether a feasible flow exists, within 26 (S + 2)(V + F + 2) steps; (4) a program prints, for each vertex of a digraph with n vertices, m arcs and natural lengths, its distance from a source capped at a given value INF (so INF for unreachable vertices), within (n + m + 1)(36 floor(log2 n) + 143) steps; (5) a program prints the size of a maximum matching of a bipartite graph with n vertices and m arcs within 80 (n + 1)(n + m + 1) steps; (6) there are a program and constants c and k such that, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map (loops allowed) with n darts, K vertices, natural capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks, and every word bound W >= c (7 s)^k, where s is n + K plus the total capacity plus 2, the program prints a maximum flow from the sources to the sinks, as a table of flow values together with a valid index into it for every dart, within c (n + K + 1)(floor(log2 n) + 1)^3 steps; this is the algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
